title: Proper product composite and its two-counit transpose
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F_{p^a}}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$. Use a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] with its specified canonical exchange and projection transformations [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf]. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all morphisms are separated of finite type. Integral pullbacks and tensors are completed; field operations use rationalization and common finite stages. Let $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, $n\geq1$, and let $f,g$ be proper. For $f:X\to B$, $g:Y\to B$, put $T=X\times_BY$, with projections $p:T\to X$, $q:T\to Y$, and $t=fp=gq$. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ put $F=Rf_!K$, $G=Rg_!L$, $D=Lp^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lq^*L$. Define $\Psi_g(F,L)$ to be the composite $F\otimes^LG\xrightarrow{\sigma}G\otimes^LF\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{g,L,F}}Rg_!(L\otimes^LLg^*F)\xrightarrow{Rg_!\sigma}Rg_!(Lg^*F\otimes^LL)$, and define
$$\lambda_{f,g}(K,L)=\alpha_{g,q}\circ Rg_!\bigl(\operatorname{PF}_{q,Lp^*K,L}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{f,g}(K)\otimes1_L)\bigr)\circ\Psi_g(F,L):F\otimes^LG\longrightarrow Rt_!D,$$
where $\alpha_{g,q}:Rg_!Rq_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rt_!$ is the supplied composition comparison and $\operatorname{Ex}_{f,g}:Lg^*Rf_!\to Rq_!Lp^*$ is the canonical exchange. Identify all proper compact-support images with ordinary direct images by the canonical proper normalization. Under $Lq^*\dashv Rq_*$ the transpose of
$$Lg^*F\otimes^LL\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_{f,g}\otimes1}Rq_*Lp^*K\otimes^LL\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_q}Rq_*D$$
is $Lq^*Lg^*F\otimes^LLq^*L\cong Lp^*Lf^*F\otimes^LLq^*L\xrightarrow{Lp^*\varepsilon_f\otimes1}D$. Moreover the transpose of $\lambda_{f,g}$ under $Lt^*\dashv Rt_*$ is exactly
$$c_{f,g}:Lt^*(F\otimes^LG)\cong Lp^*Lf^*F\otimes^LLq^*Lg^*G\xrightarrow{Lp^*\varepsilon_f\otimes Lq^*\varepsilon_g}D,$$
where $\varepsilon_f:Lf^*Rf_*\to1$ and $\varepsilon_g:Lg^*Rg_*\to1$ are the ordinary counits. These equalities use the signed symmetric monoidal pullback comparisons and the adjunction-compatible composition comparisons.

proof.text:
The maps $p,q$ are base changes of $g,f$, respectively, and $t=gq$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a),(b). Work in the finite-Tor categories supplied by [def-sf-datum], and use the canonical proper normalization in the statement. The identification of functors in (A4) alone is not used as an identification of arbitrary transformations. For the specified exchange, [fix-lem-exchanges](1),(4) allows the proper compactification $(\mathrm{id},f)$ in [def-exchange-projection]; its open base-change factor is the identity, so the normalized compact-support exchange is the ordinary counit mate. The projection transformations agree with the ordinary counit-defined projection maps under the proper identifications by [fix-prop-projection-formula] and [def-sf-pf]. These comparisons concern the specified transformations, including their completed and transported versions on the supplied coefficient domains.
Abbreviate $Lu^*,Ru_*,\otimes^L_\Lambda$ by $u^*,u_*,\otimes$, put $H=p^*K$, and write $b:g^*F\to q_*H$ for this exchange and $d=\pi_{q;H,L}\circ(b\otimes1_L)$. All tensor and pullback-composition comparisons below are those of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. The projection definition [def-exchange-projection] is
$$\pi_{u;V,W}=u_*a_{u;V,W}\circ\eta_{u,u_*V\otimes W},\qquad a_{u;V,W}=(\varepsilon_{u,V}\otimes1_{u^*W})\circ\mu_u.$$
Counit naturality and the triangle identity of [fix-prop-adjunctions](1) give
$$\varepsilon_{u,V\otimes u^*W}\circ u^*\pi_{u;V,W}=a_{u;V,W}.$$
Indeed naturality moves $u_*a$ past the counit, leaving $a\circ\varepsilon_{u,u^*(u_*V\otimes W)}\circ u^*\eta_{u,u_*V\otimes W}=a$. Apply this with $(u,V,W)=(q,H,L)$ and use naturality of $\mu_q$. The exchange definition gives $\varepsilon_{q,H}\circ q^*b=p^*\varepsilon_{f,K}$ under $q^*g^*\cong p^*f^*$. Therefore
$$\varepsilon_{q,D}\circ q^*d=((\varepsilon_{q,H}\circ q^*b)\otimes1_{q^*L})\circ\mu_q=(p^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes1_{q^*L})\circ\mu_q.$$
This is precisely the intermediate transpose in the statement. It is the transpose of the composite with the projection map; no transpose of the ill-typed isolated tensor of the exchange is asserted.

proof.text:
Continue in the notation and proper coordinates of Step 1. Put $a=\Psi_g(F,L)$, so $a=g_*\sigma_{L,g^*F}\circ\pi_{g;L,F}\circ\sigma_{F,G}$. Apply the projection calculation of Step 1 with $(u,V,W)=(g,L,F)$. Counit naturality and compatibility of the monoidal comparison with signed symmetry [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] give
$$\varepsilon_{g,g^*F\otimes L}\circ g^*a=\sigma_{L,g^*F}\circ(\varepsilon_{g,L}\otimes1_{g^*F})\circ\sigma_{g^*F,g^*G}=1_{g^*F}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,L}.$$
The last equality uses naturality of symmetry and $\sigma_{B,A}\circ\sigma_{A,B}=1$; thus the two signed swaps leave no residual sign. Let $c:g_*q_*\xrightarrow{\sim}t_*$ be the supplied composition comparison in the adjunction-compatible normalization specified in the statement. By the definition of $\lambda$ its ordinary expression is $c_D\circ g_*d\circ a$. The composite-counit formula of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3), equivalently the composite-adjunction pasting formula [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2), reads
$$\varepsilon_{t,D}\circ t^*c_D=\varepsilon_{q,D}\circ q^*\varepsilon_{g,q_*D}.$$
Substitution and counit naturality yield
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{t,D}\circ t^*\lambda
&=\varepsilon_{q,D}\circ q^*d\circ q^*(1_{g^*F}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,L})\\
&=(p^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes1_{q^*L})\circ(1_{p^*f^*F}\otimes q^*\varepsilon_{g,L})\\
&=p^*\varepsilon_{f,K}\otimes q^*\varepsilon_{g,L}.
\end{aligned}$$
Here Step 1 supplies the second line, with the natural monoidal and pullback-composition comparisons of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] inserted. Its source is $t^*(F\otimes G)\cong p^*f^*F\otimes q^*g^*G$ and its target is $D$. This is the displayed $c_{f,g}$. The argument uses only the supplied adjunctions and comparison maps, so applies at each coefficient stage in [def-sf-datum] and [def-exchange-projection]: completed operations at $\mathcal O_E$, rationalization at $E$, and compatible common finite stages at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. It does not infer equality of integral maps from finite reductions or use a reduction functor from a field coefficient category.
